title: `_verify_and_write` cyclomatic complexity 17 (42 lines)
detail: `_verify_and_write` (lines 389–460) has CCN=17 across 42 lines. The function handles seven distinct code paths: signature verification with/without a verifier, writing to file vs. data stream, truncation on signature failure, and write-error handling. Each branch is tightly interlocked, making exhaustive testing difficult. Fix: extract the verification path and the write path into separate private helpers.

title: File is 1248 lines (exceeds 1000-line maintainability guideline)
detail: At 1248 lines the file exceeds the maintainability threshold. It bundles the Glance client wrapper, the v2 image service, the RBD download handler, and two sets of exception translation helpers. Fix: split into focused sub-modules (e.g. `_client.py`, `_service_v2.py`, `_translate.py`).

title: Line 354: broad `except Exception` swallows error in `_try_special_handlers`
detail: `_try_special_handlers` (line 354) catches `Exception` broadly and logs it, then falls through to `return False`. The caller treats `False` as "special handling failed, fall back to Glance client" — so the actual error type and message are lost, making it impossible to distinguish a transient Ceph connection failure from a code bug. Note: the other five broad catches in this file (lines 249, 302, 377, 440, 696) all call `_reraise_translated_*` or `excutils.save_and_reraise_exception()` and are intentional. Fix: catch the specific exception type(s) expected from the special handlers and re-raise others.

title: Line 793: `lstrip("property-")` strips individual characters, not the prefix string
detail: `filter_.lstrip("property-")` strips any leading character in the set {'p','r','o','e','t','y','-'} from the key, not the literal prefix "property-". For a property filter key like "property-type" or "property-port", all characters in "type"/"port" fall within that set, so lstrip removes them too, producing an empty string and silently mapping the filter to the wrong key. Fix: `filter_[len("property-"):]` or `filter_.removeprefix("property-")` (Python 3.9+).

title: 4× inconsistent return statements (R1710) — functions at lines 144, 359, 389, 564
detail: Four methods have code paths that return a value and paths that fall off the end implicitly (lines 144, 359, 389, 564). Callers that do not check for `None` will hit an `AttributeError` on the implicit path. Fix: add explicit `return None` on all implicit paths, or ensure all paths return a consistent type.

title: 5× exception raised without `from` in except block (W0707, lines 730, 732, 762, 764, 1058)
detail: At lines 730, 732, 762, 764, and 1058, a Nova exception is raised inside an `except` block without `raise ... from exc`. The original Glance HTTP exception traceback is discarded, making it harder to diagnose which Glance call failed. Fix: `raise NovaException(...) from exc` at each site to preserve the exception chain.

title: Line 413: `open(dst_path, "wb")` without context manager — file may leak on exception
detail: `data = open(dst_path, "wb")` at line 413 uses a manual `close_file` boolean to track closure rather than a `with` statement. If an exception is raised before `data.close()` is reached, the file handle leaks. Fix: use `with open(dst_path, "wb") as data:` and restructure the surrounding block.

title: Lines 981, 988: `exc_type` captured from `sys.exc_info()` but never used
detail: Both `_reraise_translated_image_exception` and `_reraise_translated_exception` destructure `sys.exc_info()` into `(exc_type, exc_value, exc_trace)` but only use `exc_value` and `exc_trace`. `exc_type` is redundant here (it equals `type(exc_value)`). Fix: use `_, exc_value, exc_trace = sys.exc_info()` to make the intent clear.
